title: SOQL clauses, relationship queries, aggregate queries, bind variables, and dynamic SOQL
objectives: Write static SOQL in Apex with SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and related clauses.
Choose child-to-parent paths versus parent-to-child subqueries using relationship names.
Use aggregate functions with GROUP BY and read AggregateResult, and bind Apex variables with a colon.
Use Database.query for dynamic SOQL with binds, and refuse string-concatenated user input.
diagnostic_question: A trigger must load LAB_Stop__c children for every LAB_Shipment__c in Trigger.new, count stops per shipment, and optionally filter by a user-supplied status string. Which SOQL shape, bind, and dynamic-SOQL rule would you apply before writing a query-in-a-loop?
definition: SOQL is the query language Apex uses to retrieve sObjects. Clauses shape the result; relationship queries walk parent or child paths; aggregate queries roll up with functions such as COUNT and SUM; bind variables inject Apex values safely with a colon; dynamic SOQL builds a query string at runtime via Database.query. ([SOQL and SOSL Queries](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_SOQL.htm); [Dynamic SOQL](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_dynamic_soql.htm))
why_it_matters: Most governor failures start as SOQL in a loop or as string-concatenated filters. Interviewers want selective WHERE clauses, relationship queries instead of N+1, binds instead of injection, and a clear split between static SOQL and Database.query.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a restaurant ticket rail. SELECT is the dishes, FROM is the station, WHERE is the table filter, ORDER BY/LIMIT is how tickets are stacked. A relationship query is asking the grill for the table's sides in one walk. Aggregates are the nightly totals, not every plate. A bind is filling in table 12 from the host stand without rewriting the ticket. Dynamic SOQL is composing a ticket from a template—still use binds, never paste the diner's handwriting into SQL.
deeper_explanation: In Apex, static SOQL lives in square brackets and returns a List of sObjects, a single sObject, or an Integer for COUNT(). WITH USER_MODE appears in current guide examples; treat user-mode enforcement as neighboring APEX-014. ([SOQL and SOSL Queries](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_SOQL.htm))

Child-to-parent uses the relationship path (Contact.Account.Name). Parent-to-child uses a nested SELECT on the child relationship name. Those names come from schema (APEX-002), not from labels. ([Understanding Foreign Key and Parent-Child Relationship SOQL Queries](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_SOQL.htm))

Aggregate functions such as COUNT, SUM, and MAX return AggregateResult rows and typically need GROUP BY for non-aggregated fields. They summarize; they do not replace a list query when you need every child row. ([Working with SOQL Aggregate Functions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_SOQL.htm))

Bind variables use :apexVariable inside static SOQL and can be used with Database.query. Dynamic SOQL is a string at runtime—flexible and injection-prone if you concatenate unsanitized input. Prefer binds. Numeric SOQL governor ceilings belong to APEX-007; quote them only from that limits page.

mental_model.analogy: A restaurant ticket rail: dishes, stations, table filters, and the host-stand table number.
useful_mapping: SELECT/FROM/WHERE → dishes, station, table filter on the ticket
ORDER BY / LIMIT → how tickets are stacked and capped
relationship query → one walk to the grill for sides (parent or children)
aggregate query → nightly totals, not every plate
bind variable → host fills table 12 without rewriting the ticket
dynamic SOQL → composing a ticket from a template string at runtime
where_it_breaks: SOQL is not a full SQL dialect—no arbitrary JOINs across unrelated objects.
Aggregates return AggregateResult, not the original sObject type.
Binds are not a substitute for a selective index; large scans still hurt.
The analogy does not encode heap, query rows, or trigger bulkification.

teach_back_prompt: Explain static SOQL versus Database.query to a teammate using the ticket-rail idea, then state one place the restaurant analogy breaks.

review_schedule.prompt: Write SELECT/FROM/WHERE plus a colon bind from memory.
Given Trigger.new shipments, sketch one parent-to-child query—not a loop of queries.
When do you use AggregateResult versus a list of sObjects?
Rewrite a concatenated WHERE string to use a bind in Database.query.
Two-minute interview: relationship query versus SOSL versus aggregate.

claims.claim: Apex evaluates SOQL in square brackets; statements return a list of sObjects, a single sObject, or an Integer for count method queries.
claims.validation: SOQL and SOSL Queries in the Apex Developer Guide.

claims.claim: Dynamic SOQL creates a SOQL string at runtime (Database.query). Concatenating unsanitized input is an injection risk; prefer bind variables.

claims.claim: Very large SOQL result sets can exceed heap; a SOQL query for loop processes batches via query/queryMore. Triggers should use selective filters on indexed fields.

telugu_glossary.telugu: కోలన్‌తో Apex విలువను SOQLలోకి సురక్షితంగా పంపడం.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Static SOQL sits in brackets. Use relationship queries instead of query-per-row, aggregates when you need totals, and colon binds for Apex values. Dynamic SOQL is Database.query—bind, do not concatenate user text.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from bulk: one SOQL for Trigger.new Ids, parent paths or child subqueries as needed. Aggregates when the question is a count or sum, not a list of sObjects. Binds keep filters injection-safe in static and dynamic SOQL. If the SELECT list is runtime-driven, Database.query with binds—not string-glued WHERE. Heap pressure gets a SOQL for loop; governors are APEX-007. I will not invent query-row numbers unless I am citing the limits page.

terminology.plain: The query language Apex uses to read Salesforce records.
terminology.precise: Salesforce Object Query Language. In Apex, static SOQL is written in square brackets and returns sObjects, a single sObject, or COUNT() as Integer.
terminology.example: List<Account> rows = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Name = :labName];
terminology.non_example: SOSL FIND, which searches the text index across objects.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SQL JOIN: SOQL uses relationship paths and subqueries, not arbitrary joins.

terminology.plain: A section of the query such as WHERE, ORDER BY, or LIMIT.
terminology.precise: The parts that choose fields, object, filters, grouping, sort, and row cap. Grammar details live in the SOQL Reference.
terminology.example: WHERE Status__c = :st ORDER BY CreatedDate LIMIT 200
terminology.non_example: An Apex if statement that filters a list already in memory.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SOSL IN/RETURNING clauses, which are search syntax.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent undocumented SQL clauses.

terminology.plain: SOQL that walks parent or child records using relationship names.
terminology.precise: Child-to-parent field paths (Account.Name from Contact) or parent-to-child nested SELECT on the child relationship name.
terminology.example: SELECT Name, (SELECT Name FROM LAB_Stops__r) FROM LAB_Shipment__c WHERE Id IN :ids
terminology.non_example: A for-loop that queries children once per parent Id.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SOSL returning multiple objects that are not related.

terminology.plain: SOQL that summarizes with COUNT, SUM, MAX, and similar functions.
terminology.precise: Queries that return AggregateResult (except COUNT() which can return Integer). Non-aggregated fields typically require GROUP BY.
terminology.example: SELECT LAB_Shipment__c, COUNT(Id) cnt FROM LAB_Stop__c GROUP BY LAB_Shipment__c
terminology.non_example: SELECT Id FROM LAB_Stop__c when you needed a count per parent.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Roll-up summary fields: declarative, not Apex SOQL.
terminology.boundary: You cannot treat AggregateResult as LAB_Stop__c.

terminology.plain: An Apex value plugged into SOQL with a colon.
terminology.precise: Using :variable (including collections for IN) so the platform binds the value instead of concatenating it into the query string.
terminology.boundary: Binds do not make a non-selective filter selective.

terminology.plain: Building the query string at runtime.
terminology.precise: Database.query (and related APIs) executing a SOQL string constructed in Apex. Use for runtime field lists; bind values rather than concatenating user input.
terminology.example: Database.query('SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = :labName');
terminology.non_example: Static [SELECT Id FROM Account] in brackets.
terminology.boundary: Injection and WITH USER_MODE details still need current-guide verification.

mechanics.trigger: Need to read records in an Apex class or trigger
mechanics.before: Fields and object may or may not be known
mechanics.observe: The query compiles or the string is built with binds

mechanics.before: Unfiltered SELECT on a large object
mechanics.after: Indexed, selective filters especially in triggers
mechanics.observe: Query plan or volume test in sandbox
mechanics.failure: Leading NOT EQUALS or empty-string inequality on large objects

mechanics.before: Temptation to query in a loop
mechanics.after: One parent-to-child subquery or one grouped aggregate
mechanics.observe: Single SOQL in debug logs for the bulk path
mechanics.failure: COUNT in a loop of parent Ids

mechanics.trigger: Filter uses an Apex variable or collection
mechanics.after: Colon bind in static or dynamic SOQL
mechanics.observe: Correct rows; no quotes glued around user input
mechanics.failure: String concatenation that breaks on apostrophes

when_to_use: When an Apex class or trigger must read Salesforce rows with SOQL clauses rather than loading every record into a list.
When relationship queries can replace a SOQL-in-loop over parent Ids for child or parent fields.
When aggregate queries answer a COUNT/SUM question without returning every sObject.
When bind variables or dynamic SOQL (Database.query) must pass Apex values without concatenating user input.
when_not_to_use: Do not use SOQL when SOSL is the right tool because you only have a keyword and do not know the object (APEX-004).
Do not use aggregate queries when a trigger needs each child sObject for DML.
Do not use dynamic SOQL merely to avoid typing a static query in an Apex class.
Do not treat this SOQL-clauses lesson as a governor-number catalog (APEX-007) or as DML/Database methods (APEX-005).
configuration_or_code_location: Apex class or trigger in a disposable sandbox.
Query Editor in Developer Console for shaping SOQL before pasting into Apex.
Debug logs: SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN to count queries.
Object Manager for child relationship names used in subqueries.

worked_example.scenario: A sandbox trigger handler receives up to a batch of LAB_Shipment__c records. It must load child LAB_Stop__c rows, count stops per shipment for a log line, and optionally filter stops by a status string from a custom metadata test flag. No production data.
inputs: Optional String statusFilter from test configuration
Child relationship LAB_Stops__r confirmed in schema

decisions.decision: One parent-to-child relationship query keyed by Id IN :shipmentIds.
decisions.because: Avoids SOQL in a loop over Trigger.new.
decisions.rejected: Query stops inside for (LAB_Shipment__c s : Trigger.new)

decisions.decision: Separate aggregate COUNT grouped by LAB_Shipment__c when only totals are needed for the log.
decisions.because: Aggregates return AggregateResult, not stop rows.
decisions.rejected: Using COUNT() as if it returned LAB_Stop__c records to update

decisions.decision: Bind :statusFilter; if the SELECT list must vary, Database.query with the same bind.
decisions.because: Dynamic SOQL plus concatenation of status would be injection-prone.

configuration_or_code: List<LAB_Shipment__c> rows = [SELECT Id, (SELECT Id, Name FROM LAB_Stops__r WHERE Status__c = :statusFilter) FROM LAB_Shipment__c WHERE Id IN :shipmentIds];
List<AggregateResult> counts = [SELECT LAB_Shipment__c, COUNT(Id) cnt FROM LAB_Stop__c WHERE LAB_Shipment__c IN :shipmentIds GROUP BY LAB_Shipment__c];
If fields are runtime-only: Database.query('SELECT Id FROM LAB_Stop__c WHERE LAB_Shipment__c IN :shipmentIds');
worked_example.output: Children load in one SOQL; counts available as AggregateResult; user-supplied status never concatenated.
verification: Debug log shows one relationship query for the bulk handler, not one per shipment.
A statusFilter containing a quote still binds and does not break the query.
AggregateResult.get('cnt') is read; no cast to LAB_Stop__c.
worked_example.self_explanation: Relationship SOQL for rows, aggregate for totals, binds for Apex values, dynamic SOQL only if the shape is runtime-driven.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; Account/Contact or LAB_ objects; synthetic names only.
starting_state_checks: You can run anonymous Apex and create test Accounts.
steps: Insert two LAB_ or Account parents and several children.
Write static SOQL with a colon bind on a Set<Id> and a parent-to-child subquery.
Write an aggregate COUNT GROUP BY parent Id and print AggregateResult.
Write Database.query using the same bind; then write a bad concatenated version in a comment and explain why it is refused.
guided_completion: If you queried inside a for-loop, rewrite to Id IN :ids.
If COUNT() was assigned to List<Contact>, switch to Integer or AggregateResult.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Add ORDER BY CreatedDate LIMIT 50 to the child subquery and explain how LIMIT applies to the nested query.
evidence: Anonymous Apex output of child names and counts.
One written sentence: binds not concatenation.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete LAB_ test rows and Apex used only for this lab.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Does not prove index selectivity on a million-row object or user-mode FLS.

decision_table.signal: Object and fields are known; you need matching rows in an Apex class.
decision_table.choose: Static square-bracket SOQL with clauses and colon binds.
decision_table.not: Database.query of a fully hardcoded string.
decision_table.why: Static SOQL is compile-checked and is the default embedding in Apex.

decision_table.signal: You need children of every parent in Trigger.new.
decision_table.choose: One relationship query: WHERE Id IN :ids plus a child subquery.
decision_table.not: SOQL inside a for-loop over Trigger.new.
decision_table.why: Relationship queries plus binds are the bulk pattern; loops blow query governors (APEX-007).

decision_table.signal: You only need a count or sum per parent, not child field updates.
decision_table.choose: Aggregate SOQL with GROUP BY returning AggregateResult.
decision_table.not: Querying every child sObject just to count in Apex.
decision_table.why: Aggregate functions exist to roll up without hydrating every row.

decision_table.signal: The SELECT list or object API name is only known at runtime.
decision_table.choose: Dynamic SOQL via Database.query with bind variables.
decision_table.why: The Dynamic SOQL topic exists for runtime strings; concatenation is injection-prone.

limitations: Does not list numeric SOQL governor ceilings except by pointing to APEX-007.
Does not replace SOSL for unknown-object keyword search.
Does not teach DML or Database.setSavepoint.
Selectivity thresholds are system-defined and can change.
security_notes: Never concatenate unsanitized user input into dynamic SOQL.
WITH USER_MODE / stripInaccessible are neighboring APEX-014 concerns.
Use LAB_ data only in examples.
common_mistakes: SOQL inside a for-loop over Trigger.new.
Casting AggregateResult to the source sObject type.
Forgetting to SELECT a relationship field before touching it in Apex.
Using SOSL FIND syntax inside a SOQL query.

troubleshooting.symptom: SObject row was retrieved via SOQL without querying the requested field.
check: Add the field or relationship path to SELECT.
Nested subquery fields are selected inside the parentheses.

troubleshooting.symptom: Illegal assignment from List<AggregateResult> to List<Account>.
check: Aggregates return AggregateResult (COUNT() may return Integer).
Do not GROUP BY if you needed full sObjects.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The compiler is wrong about types.

troubleshooting.symptom: Query works in Query Editor but fails in Apex with a bind.
check: Colon binds exist only in Apex, not in all Query Editor contexts.
Collection binds require a Set/List in Apex scope.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The WHERE clause itself is invalid.

production_notes: Prefer static SOQL; use dynamic SOQL when the shape must vary.
In triggers, filter on indexed fields; see Very Large SOQL Queries.
No production deployment is authorized by this lesson.

mcqs.prompt: How does Apex embed static SOQL?

options.A: Square brackets that return sObjects, a single sObject, or COUNT() as Integer
options.B: Only as a JSON string posted to REST

mcqs.rationale: The Apex SOQL topic states statements evaluate to a list, a single sObject, or Integer for count method queries.

distractor_explanations.B: REST is not required for in-Apex SOQL.
distractor_explanations.D: FIND braces are SOSL in the API, not Apex SOQL.

mcqs.prompt: What does a colon before an Apex variable do in SOQL?

options.A: Binds the Apex value into the query

mcqs.rationale: Bind variables inject Apex values (including collections for IN) instead of concatenating strings.

distractor_explanations.D: Sharing keywords are on the class.

mcqs.prompt: You need all child stops for every shipment in a Set<Id>. Best SOQL shape?

options.A: One relationship query with a child subquery and Id IN :ids
options.B: A SOQL query inside for (Id id : ids)
options.D: Schema describe of the child object

mcqs.rationale: Parent-to-child relationship queries plus binds are the bulk pattern.

distractor_explanations.C: SOSL is text search, not Id children.

mcqs.prompt: A query uses SUM(Amount) and AccountId. What is typically required?

options.A: GROUP BY AccountId and read AggregateResult

mcqs.rationale: Aggregate functions roll up; non-aggregated fields belong in GROUP BY; results are AggregateResult.

distractor_explanations.B: Opportunity is not the aggregate type.

mcqs.prompt: Why is concatenating userInput into Database.query dangerous?

options.A: It is injection-prone; bind the value instead
options.D: User input is always a governor limit

mcqs.rationale: Dynamic SOQL exists for runtime strings; values should be bound, not glued into the WHERE clause.

distractor_explanations.B: Database.query is the dynamic SOQL API.
distractor_explanations.C: Binds are the recommended injection control.
distractor_explanations.D: Injection is a security issue, not a limit number.

mcqs.prompt: COUNT() in static Apex SOQL can return which type according to the guide?
mcqs.rationale: The SOQL topic shows Integer i = [SELECT COUNT() FROM Contact ...].

distractor_explanations.B: COUNT() is not a list of Accounts.

mcqs.prompt: A query returns so many sObjects that heap is exceeded. What does the large-query topic recommend first?

options.A: A SOQL query for loop (query/queryMore batches), or Batch Apex for mass update
options.C: Switch the query to SOSL FIND
options.D: Put the query inside another for-loop

mcqs.rationale: Working with Very Large SOQL Queries recommends SOQL for loops and notes Batch Apex as preferred for mass update.

distractor_explanations.C: SOSL does not fix heap of a huge SOQL list.

mcqs.prompt: Contact.Account.Name in SOQL is which relationship direction?
mcqs.rationale: Dot-notation from child to parent is the foreign-key path.

distractor_explanations.B: Parent-to-child uses nested SELECT on the child relationship name.

mcqs.prompt: When should you choose dynamic SOQL over static SOQL?

options.A: When the object or field list is only known at runtime
options.B: Whenever you see a bind variable
options.C: Because static SOQL cannot use WHERE

mcqs.rationale: Dynamic SOQL is for runtime query strings. Static SOQL already supports binds and WHERE.

distractor_explanations.D: Dynamic SOQL is not a sharing bypass lesson.

mcqs.prompt: Which is a SOQL clause, not a SOSL clause?
mcqs.rationale: GROUP BY belongs to SOQL aggregates. FIND/RETURNING/IN ... FIELDS are SOSL.

distractor_explanations.D: IN NAME FIELDS is SOSL field scope.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement separates SOQL in an Apex class from business data?

options.A: Deploying the class metadata does not insert the rows the SOQL would return
options.B: SOQL results are metadata and the .cls file is data
options.D: AggregateResult is a custom object definition

mcqs.rationale: The class is metadata. Queried rows are business data.

distractor_explanations.D: AggregateResult is a platform type for query results.

mcqs.prompt: The large-query topic says trigger SOQL should be what?

options.A: Selective, especially with filters on indexed fields

mcqs.rationale: For best performance, SOQL queries must be selective, particularly inside triggers.

distractor_explanations.B: That is the anti-pattern on large objects.

flashcards.back: Salesforce Object Query Language embedded in square brackets (static) or Database.query (dynamic) to retrieve sObjects.
SELECT, FROM, WHERE, plus ORDER BY, LIMIT, GROUP BY as needed.

flashcards.front: How do you bind an Apex variable in SOQL?
flashcards.back: Prefix with a colon, for example WHERE Id IN :ids.
Child-to-parent uses a field path like Account.Name. Parent-to-child uses a nested SELECT on the child relationship name.

flashcards.front: What type do SUM/COUNT grouped queries return?
flashcards.back: AggregateResult (COUNT() without GROUP BY can return Integer in Apex).
Database.query with a SOQL string built at runtime.

flashcards.front: Why not concatenate user input into dynamic SOQL?
flashcards.back: It is injection-prone. Bind the Apex value with a colon instead.

flashcards.front: SOQL in a loop over Trigger.new?
flashcards.back: Anti-pattern. Query once with Id IN :Trigger.new and relationship subqueries.

flashcards.front: Heap blown by a huge SOQL list?
flashcards.back: Use a SOQL for loop (queryMore batches) or Batch Apex for mass updates.
Selective, with filters on indexed fields when querying large objects.
SOQL queries a known object with structured filters. SOSL searches the text index, often across objects.
Relationship or list SOQL returning LAB_Stop__c, not an aggregate COUNT.

flashcards.front: Need only how many stops per shipment?
flashcards.back: Aggregate COUNT GROUP BY parent Id; read AggregateResult.
Dynamic SOQL with Database.query and binds—not concatenation.

interview_questions.question: How does SOQL run inside Apex, and what can it return?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Static SOQL sits in square brackets and returns a list of sObjects, one sObject, or Integer for COUNT(). Dynamic SOQL uses Database.query on a string.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write static SOQL when the shape is known. I bind Apex variables with a colon. I use relationship queries for parent/child and aggregates when I need rollups. I reach for Database.query only when the SELECT list or type is runtime-driven, still with binds. I keep governor numbers for APEX-007 unless I am citing the limits page.
interview_questions.example: List<Account> a = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = :labName];
follow_ups: When does SOQL return a single sObject versus a list?

interview_questions.question: Explain bind variables versus string concatenation.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A colon bind injects an Apex value safely. Concatenating user text into Database.query is injection-prone and breaks on quotes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I bind collections for IN clauses from Trigger.new. In dynamic SOQL I still bind values even if the field list is concatenated from an allowlist. I never take a raw filter string from the UI and glue it into WHERE. Binds are not a selectivity strategy—indexes still matter.
tradeoffs: Allowlisted field names vs bound values
follow_ups: Can you bind in Query Editor?

interview_questions.question: A trigger queries children inside a for-loop over Trigger.new. How do you fix it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Collect Ids, then one relationship query or one child query with parent Id IN :ids. No SOQL inside the loop.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: This is the bulk SOQL pattern interviewers expect. I sketch SELECT Id, (SELECT ... FROM Children__r) FROM Parent WHERE Id IN :Trigger.new. If I only need counts, I switch to aggregate GROUP BY. I mention selectivity for large objects. I do not quote unofficial query limits unless citing APEX-007.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Shipment__c with nested LAB_Stops__r for all Trigger.new Ids.
tradeoffs: Nested subquery vs separate child query into a Map
follow_ups: How do you map children by parent Id?
What if the child relationship name is wrong?
weak_answer_warnings: Adding LIMIT 1 inside the loop as a 'fix'

interview_questions.question: You need the number of open cases per account in Trigger.new. SOQL choice?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Aggregate COUNT with GROUP BY AccountId WHERE AccountId IN :ids, then read AggregateResult. Do not hydrate every Case unless you must update them.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate 'need rows to DML' from 'need a number.' Aggregates return AggregateResult—I get('expr0') or an alias. If I later need case fields, I switch to a relationship subquery. I keep this distinct from roll-up summary fields, which are declarative.
interview_questions.example: SELECT AccountId, COUNT(Id) cnt FROM Case WHERE AccountId IN :ids AND IsClosed = false GROUP BY AccountId
follow_ups: How do aliases work on AggregateResult?

interview_questions.question: When do you choose dynamic SOQL?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the object or field list is only known at runtime. Otherwise static SOQL. Always bind values; allowlist field names if they come from users.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: ISV field-set UIs and generic inspectors are the usual justification. A hardcoded Account service should stay static. Dynamic SOQL is not a way to skip sharing or FLS—that is APEX-014. I mention SOQL for loops if the dynamic query might return a huge heap.
interview_questions.example: Database.query('SELECT ' + allowlistedFields + ' FROM Account WHERE Name = :labName')
tradeoffs: Field sets vs fully dynamic strings
weak_answer_warnings: Using dynamic SOQL for every query

interview_questions.question: How do relationship queries differ from SOSL?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Relationship SOQL walks known parent/child schema paths on a known object. SOSL searches the text index and can return several objects that may not be related.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If I know I need LAB_Stop__c children of these shipment Ids, that is SOQL. If a user types 'acme' and I do not know whether it lives on Account, Contact, or a custom object, that is SOSL (APEX-004). Interviewers fail people who FIND when they should WHERE Id IN.
interview_questions.example: Nested SELECT on LAB_Stops__r versus FIND 'acme*' RETURNING Account, Contact.
follow_ups: Can SOSL use relationship queries when enabled?

interview_questions.question: Apex throws that a field was not queried. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The field or relationship path is missing from SELECT. Add it, or query it in the nested subquery. Describe will not hydrate it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce with the exact SOQL. Parent paths must be selected to use them in Apex. Child subquery fields are selected inside the parentheses. If the code used get('Name') on a generic sObject from a dynamic query, the string SELECT list must include Name. I do not catch this as DmlException.
interview_questions.example: Contact queried without Account.Name then c.Account.Name in Apex.
tradeoffs: Static SOQL vs dynamic field list

interview_questions.question: Your SOQL is non-selective in a trigger on a large object. What do you change first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Filter on indexed fields (Id, lookup, External Id, and others listed in the large-query topic) and reduce rows. Do not scan the whole object.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Working with Very Large SOQL Queries: selective means an indexed filter that reduces rows below a system threshold. I avoid leading NOT EQUALS and empty-string comparisons on huge objects. I bind Trigger.new Ids. If I still need millions of rows, that is Batch Apex, not a trigger query. I will not invent a 10% number in an interview unless I am quoting that page's best-practice wording and noting it can change.
interview_questions.example: WHERE Id IN :Trigger.new instead of WHERE Name != ''.
